newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai baht leads regionals lower.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai baht leads regionals lower.

text.p: Regional currencies came under assault from foreign fund sales on Wednesday, led early by dumping of the Thai baht, dealers said.
The Asian morning session was highlighted by a series of central bank interventions to defend the currencies, leading to flight-to-quality buying, they said
Rising concerns about the slowing Thai economy and rumours of political turmoil within the cabinet, seen hampering effective monetary policy, triggered baht sales for dollar.
The baht was quoted at 26.000/26.050 to the dollar compared with 25.900/25.910 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the Bank of Thailand fixing the mid-rate at 25.86 did not prevent the rate slipping to 26.03
"There was a lot of stop-loss and panic-selling which caused the market to trade 20 satangs above the fixing," a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore said.
In Malaysia, the ringgit continued to weaken pressured by ringgit/Sing sales and despite alleged central bank intervention.
"Foreign funds have been aggressive in ringgit/Sing as well, which brought Bank Negara in around the 20 level," said another dealer based in Singapore.
Bank Negara was said to have intervened at 2.5220 using large local and foreign banks to sell dollars.
At 0430 GMT, the ringgit held at 2.5230/40 against an early 2.5208 level.
It fell to as low as 2.5237, its lowest level since January 6 when it traded at 2.5235.

The currency started its meltdown on Tuesday largely due to commercial dollar buying thought to be related to a major telecommunications deal in which a U.S.-Malaysia consortium had to pay US$1 billion to South Africa's telecommunications authority, Telkom.
Elsewhere, Singapore's central bank was also seen stepping in to prevent the rise of the Singapore dollar amid dollar demand and ringgit sales, dealers said.
The rise of the Sing dollar initially was also attributed to flight from other regional currencies.
The Sing dollar was at 1.4355/65 against the U.S. dollar compared with 1.4330 late Tuesday.
Dealers said generally weak ringgit/Sing cross, hovering around 56.86/90, was also lending support.
Weakness in the baht also spilled over to Indonesia's rupiah, hurt by ample supply and jitters over an election campaign which held some potential for political disturbance.
Support, however, was seen coming from tighter liquidity later this week due to demand for weekly tax payments on Friday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,433.50/4.50 at 0430 GMT against an opening of 2,430.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore
